title: Joint Egyptian-Chinese statement: Palestinian cause is central in Middle East
summary:
Joint Egyptian-Chinese statement: Palestinian cause is central in Middle East

Chinese President Xi Jinping and Egyptian President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi reiterated that the Palestinian question remains at the core of the Middle East issue in a joint statement on Wednesday following Xi's state visit to Cairo.

In the statement, the two heads of state also reaffirmed support for the establishment of an independent State of Palestine that enjoys full sovereignty based on the 1967 borders and with East Jerusalem as its capital.

The visit coincided with the commemoration of the 70th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations between the two countries.

title: Trump suggests renaming Strait of Hormuz 'Trump Strait'
summary:
Trump suggests renaming Strait of Hormuz 'Trump Strait'

US President Donald Trump suggested renaming the Strait of Hormuz the "Trump Strait" in a post to Truth Social on Wednesday, despite control of the waterway remaining contested amid the US war on Iran.

"Now that we have it under U.S.A. control, should we change the name Hormuz Strait to TRUMP STRAIT??? Like America itself, it would be 'hotter' than ever before!" he said.

It is the latest geographical name change floated by Trump and comes a week after he ordered Lake Ontario to be renamed as "Lake America".

title: US a ‘source of regional insecurity’, Iran’s chief negotiator says
summary:
US a ‘source of regional insecurity’, Iran’s chief negotiator says

Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf said that the US is a “source of regional insecurity” during a meeting with Hamas’s head of communications on Wednesday, according to Iran's Fars news agency.

Ghalibaf also called on the US to “honour their commitments” by implementing the terms of the memorandum of understanding signed in June.

He stated that Iran is not rejecting negotiations after US President Donald Trump said on Tuesday that any deal with the country “isn't worth the paper it's written on”.

title: Exclusive: Blair asked PA to remove 'Palestine' from textbooks, former UK envoy says
summary:
Exclusive: Blair asked PA to remove 'Palestine' from textbooks, former UK envoy says

Former UK Prime Minister Tony Blair was recently sent by Donald Trump's Board of Peace to ask the Palestinian Authority (PA) to replace any mention of the word "Palestine" in schoolbooks with the Jewish designation of "Samaria", Middle East Eye has heard.

Jeremy Greenstock, who was Britain's ambassador to the UN between 1998 and 2003, told MEE that Blair attempted to exert pressure on the PA and said that if it was serious about being seen by the Board of Peace as capable of reaching an agreement with Israel to end the war on Gaza, then the word "Palestine" should be erased from textbooks.

In a wide-ranging interview on the David Hearst Podcast, Greenstock said the demand was rejected by Palestinian Authority President Mahmoud Abbas.

Greenstock also said that his former boss was experiencing "difficulties" in his new role overseeing the postwar management of Gaza for the board.

"He recently, I understand, was asked by the Board of Peace to go to Ramallah and ask to remove from the Palestinian curriculum any mention of the word Palestine if they were to be treated by the Board of Peace as capable of coming to an agreement with Israel to end the current conflict that had stemmed from 7 October onwards," Greenstock said, adding that he received this information from a ministerial level source.

Read more: Exclusive: Blair asked PA to remove 'Palestine' from textbooks, former UK envoy says

title: Two Alleged ‘TeamPCP’ Hackers Arrested in Australia
summary:
Authorities in Australia have arrested two men believed to be members of TeamPCP, a prolific cybercrime and data extortion group blamed for perpetrating the longest running spree of software supply chain attacks ever.

In a statement released today, the Australian Federal Police (AFP) said two unnamed suspects from Western Australia, aged 21 and 23, were arrested in connection with a "sophisticated cybercrime syndicate that allegedly created malicious open-source software to rob thousands of global businesses."

The AFP did not name the defendants, but KrebsOnSecurity learned the 21-year-old suspect's real identity in June, and has been communicating with him ever since. This story includes interviews with TeamPCP's self-described spokesperson, and examines clues left behind by the TeamPCP leader that likely led to his undoing.

title: Two Palestinians killed in Israeli attacks in northern and central Gaza
summary:
Two Palestinians killed in Israeli attacks in northern and central Gaza

A Palestinian youth was killed on Wednesday in an Israeli drone strike on al-Hawja in ​​Jabalia refugee camp in northern Gaza, while a Palestinian woman succumbed to her injuries after being shot by Israeli forces in Deir al-Balah in central Gaza, Wafa news reported, citing medical sources.

Medical sources at al-Shifa Hospital in western Gaza City reported the arrival of the body of a Palestinian youth and a wounded person following the Israeli strike on al-Hawja.

title: Iran seizes ship smuggling fuel in Gulf
summary:
Iran seizes ship smuggling fuel in Gulf

Iranian border guards seized a vessel with 382,000 litres of smuggled fuel in the northern Gulf, and arrested its foreign crew of 11, Iran's IRIB news agency reported on Wednesday, without specifying their nationalities.

Saudi Arabia accused Iran of attacking a tanker in the Strait of Hormuz, leading to "fatalities" among the crew, earlier on Wednesday.

title: Israel vows to retaliate if UK imposes sanctions
summary:
Israel vows to retaliate if UK imposes sanctions

Submitted by Nadav Rapaport on Wed, 09/02/2026 - 13:58
London threatens 'comprehensive' sanctions over Israel's plan to expand settlements in Area E1
A picture taken from the E1 corridor, a super-sensitive area of the occupied West Bank, shows the Israeli settlement of Maale Adumim in the background on 16 April 2025 (AFP)
Off

Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Sa'ar warned that Israel would retaliate should the UK imposed sanctions over illegal settlements in the occupied West Bank.

During an interview with Israeli news outlet Ynet on Tuesday, Sa'ar was asked about the tense relationship between Israel and the UK over recent Israeli plans to further expand settlements.

Sa'ar accused the Labour government of "acting systematically against Israel", adding that it has "already harmed defence exports to us and imposed sanctions on ministers".

In June 2025, London imposed sanctions on Israeli far-right ministers Itamar Ben Gvir and Bezalel Smotrich for inciting settler violence against Palestinians during Israel's genocide in Gaza.

"If Britain acts against Israel, Israel will act against Britain," Sa'ar said.

"They will be making a big mistake," he added.

He told Ynet that Israel is now bracing for UK sanctions and preparing a response.

Exclusive: UK to announce raft of new policies on Israel including settlement goods ban
Read More »

Late last month, Sa’ar and UK Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband traded barbs over Israel’s highly controversial plan to expand settlements in Area E1 in the occupied West Bank.

The proposed Israeli E1 project is designed to connect Jerusalem to Ma'ale Adumim and other settlements east of the city, carving into land on which Palestinians seek to establish their state.

On Tuesday, Miliband told British MPs that his government plan to impose "comprehensive" package of sanctions in the coming weeks. 

Miliband said Israel's new plan in area E1 "risks making a Palestinian state unviable".

"This government will not acquiesce in the destruction ​of the two-state solution," he added.

Miliband vowed the British government "will act and I will set ‌out ⁠a comprehensive set of measures in the coming weeks."

Sa’ar outright rejected Miliband’s statement, saying that "Israel will not be a passive victim of this policy" and will defend "its rights, its interests and its people".

Warnings to London

According to Israeli right-wing outlet Ma’ariv, Israel has already warned London that it would respond “substantially” if the British government imposes sanctions on Israeli settlements.

The report, published on Monday, said the nature of any retaliation has yet to be decided, with Israeli officials considering diplomatic, economic or other measures.

One measure under consideration is expelling British officials from the US-led International Gaza Support Centre (IGSC), established to monitor the Israel-Hamas ceasefire.

Last week, Israel expelled Dutch officials from the centre, over the Netherlands' recent ban on goods from illegal Israeli settlements. Earlier this year, Israel kicked Spain out of the IGSC, accusing Madrid of "obsessive anti-Israel bias".

Ma’ariv said Israel is weighing the risk that retaliation could damage long-term ties with British politicians who may return to power, as a future Conservative or Reform UK-backed government is expected to be more friendly towards Israel.

The newspaper also reported that the US administration is passing messages between the two governments and pressuring London not to impose sanctions.

title: Netanyahu: 'We are not retreating' in Gaza
summary:
Netanyahu: 'We are not retreating' in Gaza

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Wednesday visited troops in the Gaza Strip, where he vowed not to withdraw forces from their positions.

"We control the area. We are not retreating. We are staying on this line," Netanyahu said near the so-called Yellow Line which demarcates the areas under Hamas and Israeli military control. 

Reporting by AFP
